scope: FIRST independent English SCI, fidelity, text readability and applicability of approved unchanged fig-01/fig-02 inventories. All sixteen objects, including two figure and two caption objects, and all eighteen final prose paragraphs reviewed. No pixels.

bindingChecks.layoutChange: Object 8 splits the periodic-motion definition into its own English paragraph. Object 1 redistributes the definition of oscillation within its same three paragraphs. No object, source proposition or example is lost.
bindingChecks.sectionBoundaryMeaningPreserved: The boundaries still precede free-oscillation/system definitions and forced oscillations; the index shift comes only from the additional within-object paragraph.

scientificAssessment.equilibriumForcesAndTension: Static equilibrium is explicitly stated for both examples. Upward spring force or string tension balances downward weight on the same bob. This is not presented as a third-law pair or as a force balance throughout a moving pendulum's arc. The equilibrium-only wording avoids the false assertion that tension equals weight at a moving bottom crossing.
scientificAssessment.oscillationAndPeriodicity: A leftmost-to-rightmost-to-leftmost passage is a complete cycle. Exact recurrence at equal intervals defines ideal periodic motion; back-and-forth motion with decay or approximate regularity is still oscillatory. The English explicitly preserves that distinction instead of classifying all real oscillations as perfectly periodic.
scientificAssessment.chosenSystem: Internal/external classification is defined relative to which bodies the learner includes, not an intrinsic label on gravity or elasticity. The Earth footnote is retained, making gravitational restoring interaction internal to the stated pendulum system. For a bob-only system gravity would instead be external; the English does not contradict that alternative boundary.
scientificAssessment.freeDrivenAndDamping: Release after displacement without a continuing periodic driver is the free-motion case. Friction and air resistance may damp that free motion without making it driven. Sufficiently large damping may prevent an oscillation altogether; the text says these systems can oscillate, not that every damping strength guarantees back-and-forth motion. Periodic external driving distinguishes the hand/book and mechanical drive examples.
scientificAssessment.pendulumScope: The definition concerns bodies mounted so that they can oscillate under gravity. It does not assert that an arbitrary pivot through the center of gravity supplies gravitational restoring torque. Ruler and balance-beam examples are retained as bodies that can act as pendulums, not as guaranteed oscillators for every mounting.
scientificAssessment.freshEnglishClarifications: The added equal-time-interval condition, imperfect-regularity caution, nonconstant amplitude/period caution, chosen-system restoring wording, explicit damped-free distinction, and qualification of the hand's periodic motion are all scientifically justified. They clarify existing examples rather than adding a new problem, figure or curriculum topic.
scientificAssessment.readability: The demonstration sequence is concrete: set up, displace, release, observe, define. Short paragraphs separate periodicity, system boundaries and free/forced classification. Amplitude/period terminology is an added compact caution rather than a new calculation or task; the surrounding repeated-motion explanation remains understandable.
scientificAssessment.independentJudgment: The existing source/current Chinese/native delivery is not treated as historic SCI approval. The force balance, recurrence definition, system boundary and damping/driver distinctions were evaluated directly.

blockFindings.finding: Retains the prevalence of oscillation and ease of initiating it without adding a universal claim about every object.

Retains the suspended spring, metal bob, static force balance, downward displacement/release, up/down repetition, definition and eventual damping. The balance applies at equilibrium, not throughout motion. Figure 1a/b applicability is correct.
Existing fig-01 ID, structural label, source binding and placement are retained. This is applicability/identity acceptance only, not a new pixel review.
Caption text Figure 1 translates the source caption while keeping its original structural label and figure number.

Retains vertical string/tension-weight equilibrium, displaced release, pendulum definition, gravity qualification, axis wording, ruler and balance beam. Figure 2a is equilibrium and 2b represents successive positions of one fixed-length pendulum, not several different strings.

The marked Earth footnote survives. Gravity supplies restoring action for this gravitational pendulum, and Earth is explicitly included in the chosen system. It does not label gravity universally internal.
Existing fig-02 ID, label, source reference and placement remain unchanged. Approved fixed-length inventory and SVG are reused, not visually reviewed again.
Figure 2 is a faithful English caption; numeric and structural identity remain fixed.

Retains the defining repeated motion and complete left-right-left cycle. The added equal-time-interval requirement correctly specifies periodicity. The separate definition paragraph improves separation without changing object identity.
Exact or approximate repetition is preserved. The new real-oscillation regularity caution prevents equating oscillation with perfectly periodic motion.
All four examples remain: car-engine piston, buoy in waves, wind-blown branches, heart. The added amplitude/period caution is correct and introduces no replacement example.
System, internal and external forces are defined by membership of the chosen collection of bodies. The heading remains attached to the free-oscillation section.

Retains displacement from equilibrium, free oscillation, spring/string masses and lack of a periodic external force. Added release/chosen-system wording and explicit allowance for damping are correct; free is not redefined as lossless.
Retains the hand-driven book example. The periodic-movement qualifier avoids asserting that every arbitrary hand motion must be periodic; force magnitude/direction variation remains.
The forced-oscillation definition correctly specifies a periodically varying external driver, not resistance alone.
Both driven examples remain: internal-combustion-engine piston and sewing-machine needle. They need not be sinusoidal to qualify as periodically driven.

paragraphFindings.finding: Opening claims and simple vocabulary are faithful.
Spring setup and equilibrium-only F0/G balance match Figure 1a.
Pull/release and alternating vertical motion match Figure 1b; this is the retained demonstration, not a new exercise.
Oscillation definition and eventual decay are preserved together.
String tension balances weight only in the stated static equilibrium; displaced release yields damped swings.
Gravity-bound pendulum definition and footnote link remain; no arbitrary mounting is promised to oscillate.
Ruler-on-nail and balance-beam examples are both retained.
Earth is explicitly included in this gravitational oscillating system.
The leftmost-rightmost-leftmost cycle is complete; another such motion allows approximate repetition.
Exact repetition at equal intervals correctly defines periodic motion.
Real oscillation may be approximate rather than perfectly regular.
All four real-world examples survive; constant amplitude/period is not falsely required.
System-relative internal/external definitions remain distinct and clear.
Released spring/string systems and internal restoring interaction fit the chosen-system definition.
No periodic driver is required, and damping can be present during free oscillation.
The book is periodically hand-driven in this example; arbitrary hand motion is not assumed periodic.
Periodically varying external driver is the correct defining feature here.
Engine piston and sewing-machine needle are retained forced-motion examples.

figureApplicability.method: Existing approved source inventories and review bindings read as text; current spec/SVG/render/review hashes checked once. No image payload, source-pixel replay, new rendering or glyph certification.

figures.finding: Approved panel a has a suspended spring/bob with balanced upward F0 and downward G at equilibrium. Panel b has the same support, longer spring and lower bob with alternating motion arrows. English references a for force balance and b for displaced motion, with no added force value or dimension.

Approved panel a is static vertical-string equilibrium with upward tension and downward weight. Panel b shows alternative positions of the same pendulum with fixed string length and a curved trajectory. English preserves those identities and does not infer changing length, multiple bobs, measured angles or force balance throughout the arc.

research.purpose: Scientific system-boundary and damping/driver verification only, not translation research.
research.method: Official publisher pages read as rendered text through cloak-fetch, without screenshots.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 1, 15.5 Damped Oscillations
sources.support: A released mass can undergo decaying undriven oscillation; sufficiently strong damping can prevent oscillation.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 1, 9.3 Conservation of Linear Momentum
sources.support: The system is a chosen collection of bodies; including Earth changes which interactions are external, and internal forces do not imply zero force on each individual member.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 1, 15.6 Forced Oscillations
sources.support: A periodic driving force adds a driving term to the damped oscillator equation; driven motion is distinct from a released undriven system.
